Operational cards · slot 6 · design closure

Design phase closed

The expanded Process detail is withdrawn. Activity and participants now share one row — participants left, an activity trigger right — and no activity row is printed onto the card face at all. The Process card is 55px shorter. P1 stops being a blocker; G1 narrows to two cards. Eight cards LOCKED.

What was removed and why specifying it was the error

The detail surface was specified to hold five sections: process identity, the full journey, stage history, participants at their own grain, and current work. Measured against the summary, four of those five were the summary again at a larger size. Only stage history was new — and stage history is precisely the projection Alloy does not have.

A detail surface whose only original content is the content that does not exist is not a detail surface. It is a magnifying glass. The Process card is now summary-only at every placement, and there is no second representation of a process anywhere in the family.

One foot row participants left · activity right −55px

Activity and participants shared nothing, and each claimed its own band, its own top rule and its own height. They now share one row. The left half is populated only by what the rail cannot say — a scoped child with its own action, or the fact that everyone is together at one stage. When the rail has already said it, the left half is empty and the row carries the trigger alone; that is still cheaper than the two bands it replaced.

Activity on demand zero rows on the card face

The trigger carries the count, so the closed state is still informative: an operator can tell whether opening it is worth the click without opening it. The bound moved off the truth and onto the menu's height — it scrolls at 17rem rather than silently truncating the record at three, which is what the previous bounded region did.

P1 regraded blocker → future capability

P1 — a durable stage-history projection — blocked nothing that ships. The Process card never renders a historical stage fact, so its absence is invisible at every density.

It stays on the roadmap because reporting, analytics and cycle-time questions all want it, and none of those are card questions. The constraint that made it a blocker survives intact and binds whatever consumes it: entered, exited, outcome and transition render only from a projection that holds them. Skipped and reopened are never inferred, and a date is never fabricated to fill a slot. P1 must not be solved in card state.

With the Process detail gone, G1 — the 360px expanded-body cap — is relevant only to Financials and Health & Safety, the two cards that still have an expanded representation. It remains a Director decision, gating Slice 5 for those two alone.

The four layers final contract

LayerContentTruth owner
1 · IdentityProcess name, iconBusiness Process definition
2 · Journey railStages, current stage, ≤2 annotation slots per node, participant markersBusiness Process + participant process state
3 · Current workScope label, primary answer, action rowCurrent Work
4 · Foot rowParticipants left; Recent activity n ▾ right. Zero rows on the card faceThe canonical activity projection

Grain stays case — the Focus Panel is case-grain by shipped conformance test. Participant divergence projects onto the rail, which is why no children section survives below it. Densities are compact and standard; no expanded variant exists. Actions carry their subject explicitly and never infer one from selection.

Slice 1 — Attendance and Staff, read-only, registered. Both have complete canonical read truth today, no blocking gaps and no mutation dependency. They prove the whole registration path — provider, catalog, archetype, Surfaces placement — against cards whose truth already exists, before any card that needs new backend work.

Then: 2 F0 → F7 → F5 → Financials · 3 participant resolver → Process · 4 M1 → H1–H4 → Health · 5 G1 → Financials and Health expanded details · 6 S2 → S1 → Safety Signals. P1 is not in the sequence.

Design and specification are complete. The next mission is production implementation.
